ideas.title: Review of Equality, Diversity and Inclusion officer roles
alternative_routes: Workforce / establishment review by S151 + HR director
Working group with cross-portfolio remit
ideas.first_concrete_action: Cabinet directs S151/HR to scope EDI roles + report back; no jobs cut without process
opposition_counter: This is a culture-war attack on equalities duties under the Equality Act 2010.
Reform will face legal challenge from staff and equality bodies.
pre_empt_lines: The council's statutory equalities duties under the Equality Act 2010 are unchanged.
The review is into role design and headcount efficiency, not the council's compliance with the public sector equality duty.

ideas.title: Public-facing treasury management transparency report
alternative_routes: Audit Committee deep-dive scoped to historic treasury decisions
Cabinet decision commissioning S151 transparency report
Motion at Full Council if leader wants public political moment
ideas.first_concrete_action: S151 commissioned to produce a public-facing report covering historic TMS decisions, current market values, and recovery scenarios within 30 days
opposition_counter: Reform are creating market instability by panicking about routine investment performance.
The external auditor signs off the accounts every year — there is nothing to expose.
pre_empt_lines: These investments are documented in published accounts but never explained to residents.
The external auditor is contractually limited to financial-statement assurance and has not been asked to explain past investment decisions in plain English.
ideas.precedent: Lancashire CC ongoing 2026 — Cllr Atkinson press exposure of £548m → £204m fall
ideas.evidence_summary: Gateshead's long-term treasury investments fell from £${treasury_high_m}m at ${treasury_high_date} to £${treasury_low_m}m at ${treasury_low_date} — a paper loss of £${treasury_loss_m}m. The largest single holding is ${largest_holding_description}. With 30-year gilt yields at multi-decade highs, the paper losses have widened, not narrowed.

ideas.title: Public review of inherited Children's Services / SEND budget overspend
alternative_routes: Audit Committee deep-dive
Public-facing publication of historic forecasts vs outturns
Best Value review request to MHCLG
ideas.first_concrete_action: Scrutiny Chair tables a call-in within 30 days; published timeline of historic overspend forecasts vs outturns
opposition_counter: Children's services pressures are national — every authority faces them.
Reform are politicising statutory services to children at risk.
pre_empt_lines: Statutory care of children is unchanged — the review is into the previous administration's forecasting and contract management, not frontline practice.
Other Reform-controlled councils have used the same scrutiny route without disrupting frontline services.
ideas.precedent: Kent CC, ongoing — £620M children's services pressure exposed by Reform leader's day-1 review
ideas.evidence_summary: Gateshead has a recurring Children's Services / SEND-DSG overspend of £${overspend_m}m per annum. Cumulative deficit since ${deficit_start_year} is £${cumulative_deficit_m}m. The previous administration ${previous_admin_failure_summary}.

ideas.title: Cut Special Responsibility Allowances (SRAs) and freeze Members' basic allowance
alternative_routes: Independent Remuneration Panel referral with a Reform-direction submission
ideas.first_concrete_action: Refer Members' Allowances Scheme to the Independent Remuneration Panel with a Reform direction to cut SRAs by 25-50%
opposition_counter: This will deter working-class candidates from public office.
The IRP is independent — Reform are politicising it.
pre_empt_lines: The cuts apply to elected members' Special Responsibility Allowances, not the basic allowance, preserving access for working-class candidates.
The IRP remains independent — this is a direction the council is entitled to make under the Local Authorities (Members' Allowances) Regulations.
ideas.precedent: Lancashire CC May 2025 — Reform froze SRAs and committed to an IRP review; widely reported locally as a credibility signal.

ideas.title: Multi-year council tax freeze pledge tied to verifiable savings
alternative_routes: Cabinet pledge with annual confirmation at MTFS
ideas.first_concrete_action: Cabinet drafts pledge tied to procurement-savings + officer-overhead targets; motion to confirm at next Full Council
opposition_counter: This will force frontline service cuts.
Reform are making a populist promise without a deliverable plan.
pre_empt_lines: The freeze is conditional on procurement savings, officer-overhead reduction, and a published delivery plan — not magical accounting.

ideas.title: Submit Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by 19 June 2026 (unlocks 90% DSG write-off)
alternative_routes: Director of Children's Services + S151 prepare a delegated submission
Where the council is in active Safety Valve, the same plan rolls over per DfE explanatory note 9 Feb 2026
ideas.first_concrete_action: Cabinet sets a 19 June 2026 submission target; Director of Children's Services + S151 Officer co-sign approval delegation
opposition_counter: The reform plan was developed under the previous administration — Reform is taking credit.
The DSG write-off is automatic; submission is procedural.
pre_empt_lines: The 19 June deadline applies regardless of who designed the plan. Missing it would forfeit a multi-million-pound write-off.
The plan is conditional on demonstrable delivery — the new administration's job is to deliver against it, not just sign it.
ideas.precedent: HM Treasury / DfE explanatory note 9 Feb 2026; House of Commons Library briefing CBP-10485; LGC 9 Feb 2026 coverage
ideas.evidence_summary: Gateshead's DSG high-needs deficit is £${cumulative_deficit_m}m at 31 March 2026. The High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG, announced 9 Feb 2026 alongside the final 2026/27 LGFS) writes off 90% (~£${dsg_write_off_m}m) on submission of an approved Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by 19 June 2026. The residual 10% (~£${dsg_residual_m}m) remains on the council's books.

ideas.title: National anthem before every Full Council meeting
alternative_routes: Cabinet decision (faster, no opposition vote — recommended if avoiding opposition spectacle)
Civic Mayor's standing direction at the start of mayoralty
ideas.first_concrete_action: Civic Mayor publishes a chamber-procedure note on day-1, motion to formalise at next Full Council
opposition_counter: This is performative culture-war politics that does nothing for residents.
Reform are wasting council time on flag-waving while bins go uncollected.
pre_empt_lines: This council notes that residents and serving forces personnel deserve to see public institutions take national symbols seriously.
This is a no-cost change consistent with the council's existing Armed Forces Covenant obligations.
ideas.precedent: Lancashire County Council, May 2025 (proceeded by Civic Mayor's direction; widely covered locally and nationally as a Reform signature move)

ideas.title: Public publication of supplier concentration + HHI per portfolio
alternative_routes: Procurement Strategy update
ideas.first_concrete_action: Head of Procurement publishes top-25 suppliers + HHI per service area + tendering history within 60 days
ideas.evidence_summary: Gateshead has supplier concentration HHI of 142 in procurement (>0.25 = red flag). The largest single supplier is ${top_supplier} at £${top_supplier_spend_m}m / 8.2% of procurement.

ideas.title: Public publication of PFI / lease / off-balance-sheet liabilities
ideas.first_concrete_action: S151 publishes total PFI / IFRS 16 lease commitments with annual unitary charges, contract end dates, and clawback rights

facts: SOUTH TYNE & WEAR ENERGY RECOVERY LTD: £181.0M / 103 txns — waste PFI / Energy-from-Waste joint venture covering Gateshead + South Tyneside + Sunderland.
PINNACLE SCHOOLS (GATESHEAD) LTD: £59.8M / 138 txns — schools PFI Special Purpose Vehicle.
SAINT-GOBAIN BUILDING DISTRIBUTION LTD T/A JEWSON: £107.9M across 42,346 transactions — extraordinarily high transaction count for a building materials supplier; warrants ledger audit.
5 suppliers with overdue Companies House accounts (highest count among the 12 new councils). SOLEHAWK LTD + COVENT HOUSE flagged.
primary_sources: South Tyne & Wear Waste Management Partnership records

ideas.evidence_summary: Gateshead has £${pfi_liabilities_m}m in PFI / off-balance-sheet liabilities, with annual unitary charges of £${pfi_annual_m}m and contracts running to ${pfi_end_year}.

ideas.title: Fly the Union Jack permanently from the council building
